acceptance_criteria: Auto-compact health exposes a typed current episode separately from lifetime totals, with an explicit state, scope, generation, start time, last transition, and recovery evidence.
Per-scope cleanup, session replacement, and shutdown close or reset current episode state without erasing cumulative diagnostic totals.
Runtime health derives degradation only from a current unresolved auto-compact episode and cannot infer current risk from a positive lifetime counter.
The external health checker consumes the typed episode contract rather than treating every positive auto-compact integer as a generic at-risk marker.
A healthy response with only historical auto-compact totals remains healthy after the current episode has recovered.
An active rapid-rearm or ineffective-compaction episode produces a warning with bounded reason-bearing evidence and clears only after a verified recovery transition.
Counter and episode semantics are documented consistently for runtime, deployment checks, operators, and alert consumers.
Focused tests prove warning onset, historical-total non-warning, cleanup, shutdown, scope isolation, restart generation, stale episode rejection, and verified recovery.

falsifier_or_remaining_gap: The finding would be falsified if cleanup or shutdown cleared a typed current auto-compact episode, runtime and external health distinguished that current state from lifetime totals, or a healthy later-idle payload containing only historical totals remained non-warning. Exact source inspection and the direct two-sample health probe disproved those conditions. The 219 passing issue-relevant and control tests establish current behavior, not the missing episode contract. This audit did not observe a production warning, measure alert frequency, or choose episode aging thresholds, so operational incidence and alert calibration remain implementation-time measurement obligations.
impact: One historical ineffective compaction or rapid rearm can make the external health view warn indefinitely even after the session and scoped state are gone. Operators cannot distinguish an active compaction risk from harmless lifetime history, creating sticky false warnings and weakening trust in real alerts.

suggested_remediation: Model auto-compaction as a typed per-scope current episode with generation and transition evidence, separate from lifetime totals. Close current state during cleanup, replacement, and shutdown while retaining cumulative diagnostics. Make runtime and external health consume the same current-episode contract, warn only for an unresolved episode, and require a verified recovery transition before clearing it. Version or coordinate the producer and consumer change so historical totals can never be reinterpreted as current risk.
